title: Design adaptive JSON parameter schema & pragmatic validation for function-calls
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: Function/tool calling currently accepts a loose JSON blob as parameters, which causes frequent user errors, brittle downstream parsing, and surprising runtime failures. We need a compact, forward-compatible JSON schema definition format plus pragmatic runtime validation and a catalog of user-facing errors that map cleanly to developer actions.

Goals:
- Define a lightweight schema DSL (JSON-first) that can be embedded in model responses and the API model registry.
- Provide deterministic validation semantics suitable for both hosted and private deployments (no non-deterministic heuristics).
- Produce stable, actionable error messages and error codes so SDKs and client apps can present recovery flows.
- Support compatibility layers: allow older clients to interoperate with extended schemas and provide graceful fallback behavior.

Non-goals:
- Full JSON Schema v2019 feature parity. We aim for a minimal, readable subset focused on typical function-call payloads (strings, numbers, booleans, enums, arrays of primitives, optional fields, and shallow objects).

Deliverables:
- Schema DSL spec doc + examples.
- Runtime validator (JS + Go) README with validation modes (strict | tolerant | best-effort).
- Error catalog and mapping to SDK exceptions.
- Migration/compatibility guidance for existing models and tools.
tasks: Implement Go validator shim for Dedicated/Private (infra)
Create error code catalog and message templates (PM + DX)
Integrate validator into runtime hook for function-call postprocess
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published to Confluence with examples and migration notes
JS validator passes canonical test-suite (>= 95% coverage for DSL behaviors)
Runtime rejects malformed params with deterministic error code and message
SDKs map error codes to typed exceptions and include recovery hints
Compatibility mode returns legacy-compatible parameter shape when requested
decision_log: 2026-02-03: Chose a JSON-first DSL over full JSON Schema to reduce surface area for users and make model-emitted schemas readable.
2026-02-05: Validation modes finalized: strict (blocking), tolerant (warn+attempt coerce), best-effort (coerce where safe).
2026-02-10: Error codes will be namespaced under RI:VC (Redwood Inference: Validation/Contract). Example: RI:VC.MISSING_FIELD
2026-02-12: Compatibility chosen as explicit 'compatibilityVersion' field in function manifest rather than inferring from client headers to avoid silent breaking changes.
validation_error_catalog: RI:VC.MISSING_FIELD - required field '<field>' not present. Message: "Missing required parameter '<field>'." Recovery: provide the field in the parameters or mark as optional in schema.

RI:VC.TYPE_MISMATCH - field '<field>' expected <expected_type> but got <actual_type>. Message: "Parameter '<field>' expected type <expected_type> but received <actual_type>." Recovery: coerce client-side or use tolerant mode to attempt coercion.

RI:VC.ENUM_MISMATCH - field '<field>' value not in allowed set. Message: "Value for '<field>' not recognized; expected one of: <values>." Recovery: map value to allowed enum or update schema if new value is valid.

RI:VC.EXTRA_FIELDS - unexpected field(s) present. Message: "Unexpected parameter(s): <list>. By default these are ignored in tolerant/best-effort modes." Recovery: Remove unexpected fields or extend schema.
RI:VC.COERCION_FAILED - attempted coercion failed. Message: "Unable to coerce '<field>' to <expected_type>." Recovery: supply correctly typed value.
RI:VC.SCHEMA_PARSE_ERROR - schema definition invalid. Message: "Function schema could not be parsed." Recovery: correct schema manifest and redeploy.

RI:VC.COMPATIBILITY_MISMATCH - client compatibilityVersion mismatch. Message: "Client expects schema v<client> but function provided v<server>. Use compatibility flag to request legacy shape." Recovery: set compatibilityVersion in request or update client SDK.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-ambitious schema will slow model-emitted schema adoption. Mitigation: keep DSL small and readable, provide examples and a one-click migration checklist.

Risk: Validator latency impacts token streaming paths. Mitigation: implement streaming/incremental validation and benchmark in staging; default to best-effort for streaming responses and strict for post-call enforcement.
Risk: Compatibility complexity across old SDKs. Mitigation: explicit compatibilityVersion flag and server-side legacy-transformation rules to avoid implicit breaking changes.
